# COARE 3.6 reference subset for OceanMixedLayer tests (issue #38).
#
# Source: NOAA-PSL COARE algorithm, https://github.com/NOAA-PSL/COARE-algorithm
#   commit bd1cac80d2dae454e699f9ef46204dfd88086a71 (master, 2026-03-17).
#   Inputs : Python/COARE3.6/test_36_data.txt — the ship observations the
#            algorithm is distributed with (~13-15 N, 51-59 W).
#   Outputs: produced by running that commit's Python/COARE3.6/coare36vnWarm_et.py
#            (Tsea = the thermosalinograph column, ts_depth = its depth, no wave
#            input, warm layer and cool skin on), on numpy 2.4.6. Three numpy-2
#            incompatibilities in the reference code were patched without changing
#            what it computes for this data set: (1) the chained comparisons
#            `rr[iice] > np.logical_and(0.135, rr[iice]) <= 2.5` (and the 2.5/1000
#            one) in the sea-ice roughness branch, empty here; (2) `bad_input =
#            np.where(np.isnan(sw_dn) == 1)` on a scalar, a no-op here; (3)
#            `alb[k] = a[i,j]` assigning a 1x1 array.
#   NOTE: the output file shipped in that repository
#   (test_36_output_withnowavesinput_withwarmlayer.txt) is NOT reproduced by the
#   shipped code — dT_warm differs by up to 0.24 K — so it was evidently made by
#   another code version; we therefore test against the code, not that file.
# Rows: local solar days 19-25 of the record (local day = floor(jd + (lon+7.5)/15/24),
# the day definition of the COARE warm-layer loop), plus the row before them.
# Values are copied from the input file / the run output, rounded to 6-8
# significant digits; nothing here is modelled by Aeolus.
#
# jd        : day of year (UTC)                       [input col 1]
# lat, lon  : deg                                     [input cols 12,13]
# Ss        : salinity, psu                           [input col 16]
# tsnk      : sea-snake temperature (~0.05 m), degC   [input col 9]
# tsg       : thermosalinograph temperature, degC     [input col 19]
# ztsg      : thermosalinograph depth, m              [input col 20]
# lw_dn     : downwelling longwave, W m-2             [input col 11]
# usr       : friction velocity incl. gustiness, m s-1          [output col 1]
# tau       : wind stress, N m-2                                [output col 2]
# hsb, hlb  : sensible / latent heat flux, W m-2, positive up   [output cols 3,4]
# dT_skin   : cool-skin depression, K                           [output col 18]
# dz_skin   : cool-skin thickness, m                            [output col 20]
# lw_net    : net longwave, W m-2, positive heating ocean       [output col 28]
# sw_net    : net shortwave, W m-2, positive heating ocean      [output col 29]
# Le        : latent heat of vaporisation, J kg-1               [output col 30]
# rhoa      : air density, kg m-3                               [output col 31]
# hrain     : rain heat flux, W m-2, positive cooling ocean     [output col 38]
# dT_warm   : warm-layer warming, K                             [output col 51]
# dz_warm   : warm-layer thickness, m                           [output col 52]
# dT_warm_to_skin : warming between surface and ztsg, K         [output col 53]
jd lat lon Ss tsnk tsg ztsg lw_dn usr tau hsb hlb dT_skin dz_skin lw_net sw_net Le rhoa hrain dT_warm dz_warm dT_warm_to_skin
